title: Multi-modal virtual environments for education with haptic and olfactory feedback

findings.consequent: Human performance (speed and precision) in interactive tasks
findings.quote: Several experimental studies established that haptic sensations provide essential information during interactive tasks. Indeed, they have demonstrated a dramatically improved human performance in terms of speed and precision when supported by force and touch feedback (Ouh-Young et al. 1989; Richard and Coiffet 1995; Birmanns and Wriggers 2003).

findings.consequent: Misjudgment of the size of virtual objects (a disadvantage of pure visual representation)
findings.quote: Haptic rendering compensates common disadvantages of a pure visual representation, such as the misjudgment of the size of virtual objects (Wu et al. 1999).

findings.consequent: Sense of presence in virtual environments
findings.quote: Previous studies have reported that compelling olfactory cues have the potential to enhance the sense of presence (Barfield and Danas 1996; Dinh et al. 1999), invoke emotion, and provide salient spatial cues (Von Békésy 1964).

findings.antecedent: Odors (even when subjects are unaware of their presence)
findings.consequent: Performance on vigilance tasks and mathematical tasks
findings.quote: Previous studies have shown that odors, in some cases, can influence performance on vigilance tasks (Warm et al. 1990), and mathematical tasks (Baron 1990), even when the subjects are unaware of the presence of the odor (Degel and Köster 1999);
Smell-related memories have a stronger emotional content than those triggered by other sensory modalities.

findings.consequent: Mood, vigilance, stress, retention and recall of learned materials
findings.quote: According to Youngblut et al. (1996), "odors can be used to manipulate mood, increase vigilance, decrease stress, and improve retention and recall of learned materials."

findings.antecedent: Integrating many senses (multi-modal feedback) into a single display system
findings.consequent: Feeling of presence in the environment and both cognitive and sensory-motor performance
findings.quote: Integrating many senses into a single display system increases the feeling of presence in the environment and both cognitive and sensory-motor performance.

findings.consequent: Knowledge-building experiences and an alternative educational process
findings.quote: It has been suggested that immersive virtual reality (VR) technology allows knowledge-building experiences and in this way provides an alternative educational process.
Moreover, we propose that human-scale haptic interaction (SPIDAR-H) leads to better acquisition and retention thanks to bigger physical and psychic/emotional implications of the user.

findings.antecedent: Association of a specific scent with each energy level (in the Bohr atomic model)
findings.quote: Furthermore, we put forward the assumption of reification reinforcement through the association of a specific scent with each energy level linked to haptic feedback.

findings.antecedent: Association of scent with the secondary quantum number (l)
findings.consequent: Conceptualization of the orbital's shape and understanding the role of l
findings.quote: In a similar way, we make the hypothesis that a reification referring to the energy level degeneracy phenomenon and based on the association of scent with the secondary quantum number l, might support the conceptualization and shed light on the role of the second quantum number l in forming the orbital's shape.

findings.consequent: Interaction of scientists with experiments and a solid base for rationalizing micro- and nanoscopic levels
findings.quote: The use of VR tools not only enhances the interaction of scientists with the experiment by offering an easy way of virtually exploring its components but also offers a solid base for rationalizing what is happening at micro- and nanoscopic levels by providing a VR representation of its elementary components (Ihlenfeldt 1997).

A well-known example is the GROPE project that was the first to demonstrate the usefulness of haptic interfaces for the perception of force fields, and in molecular docking tasks (Ouh-Young et al. 1988; Brooks Jr et al. 1990).

findings.consequent: Time required to create a simple molecule in a VE
findings.quote: The results show that by providing force feedback, it is possible to decrease the amount of time required to create a simple molecule in a VE.

findings.antecedent: Characteristics of VR (immersion, presence, direct engagement, autonomy, interactivity)
findings.consequent: Support for learning according to a constructivist perspective
findings.quote: These features of VEs go some way in supporting learning according to a constructivist perspective for the acquisition of knowledge (Dede et al. 1997; Youngblut 1998; Roussos and Gillingham 1998; Mikropoulos et al. 1998; Winn and Windschitl 2001).

findings.consequent: Ability for educators to place students into instructional environments that are otherwise difficult or impossible to achieve
findings.quote: Moreover, VR allows educators to place their students into instructional environments, which is difficult or impossible to achieve otherwise (Ihlenfeldt 1997; Nikolou et al. 1997; Trindade et al. 1999; Sankaranarayanan et al. 2003; Sauer et al. 2004).

findings.consequent: Student enthusiasm and apparent usefulness of olfaction
findings.quote: A few students who have tried both configurations and the different interaction techniques were able to understand the haptic representation, and were enthusiastic when experiencing SPIDAR-H. Students were pleasantly surprised and impressed by the additional olfactory information, although its usefulness was not apparent to them.
